findings.title: include_website_name missing question mark — dead code
findings.body: The new `include_website_name` method is defined without the trailing `?`. Throughout this file (and AMS conventions used by Discourse), every include predicate is named `include_<attr>?` (e.g., `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_stats?`). Without the `?` the serializer never calls this method, so it has no effect and `website_name` will be included in the JSON whenever its computed value is non-nil. It should be `def include_website_name?`.

findings.title: TL0 users' website_name leaks to anonymous viewers
findings.body: `:website` is registered with `untrusted_attributes`, which auto-generates `include_website?` to return `false` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (i.e., a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous/staff-with-restriction visitor). The new `include_website_name?` predicate (or the existing `include_website_name` if it's a typo) only checks `website.present?` and never calls `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result, even when `website` is suppressed from the payload for a TL0 user, `website_name` (which still reveals the host and path the user has set) can still be serialized, bypassing the same privacy gate. Either add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call (lines 105–111) or have the include predicate return `false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: website_name drops query string and fragment
findings.body: `website_name` concatenates `URI(website).host` with `URI(website).path`, but never appends `.query` or `.fragment`. A user whose website is, e.g., `http://example.com/users/bob?tab=posts#about` will be displayed as `example.com/users/bob`, losing information the PR title advertises ('show complete URL path'). If the intent really is to mirror the original full URL when on the same domain, `URI(website).request_uri` (or host + path + query + fragment) should be used instead of just path.

findings.title: No coverage that website_name is hidden from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
findings.body: The 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context asserts that `untrusted_attributes` (`:bio_raw`, `:bio_cooked`, `:bio_excerpt`, `:location`, `:website`, `:profile_background`, `:card_background`) are absent from `json`. After this change `:website_name` carries the same private information as `:website` and must be excluded by the same `restrict_user_fields?` gate, but the existing assertion was not extended and no new test exercises this case. Without such a test the privacy regression described above can be reintroduced unnoticed.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) parsed up to three times per call
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is invoked three times inside `website_name` (once for `.host`, then again for `.path` in each branch that includes the path). Each call constructs and parses a URI object. The value should be assigned to a local once (e.g., `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused. The method is called for every user serialization, so this multiplies unnecessarily.

findings.title: Drive-by doc comment change unrelated to PR
findings.body: This PR is about changing the website display behaviour. The diff also edits the JSDoc above `profileBackground` from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground` in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6`. The fix is correct, but it's an unrelated drive-by change that should be in its own commit/PR so the website-domain UX change stays focused and reviewable.

findings.title: Subdomain check uses brittle two-segment suffix test
findings.body: The `elsif` branch only fires when `discourse_host` and `website_host` have the same number of dot-separated segments and that count is `> 2`. A case such as `Discourse.current_hostname` returning `example.com` (2 segments) while `website_host` is `forums.example.com` (3 segments) skips the `elsif`, drops into `else`, and `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)` is false, so the user sees just `forums.example.com` with no path even though the discourse host is a parent suffix of the website host. The condition that decides whether to show the path should be based purely on suffix relationship (e.g., one host ends with `.` + the other, or they are equal), not on equal segment counts, otherwise same-domain path display is missed in mixed-depth subdomain setups.
